evals.prompt: Analyze our PPTB tools and propose refactorings.
evals.expected_output: The tools under tools/ that have a package.json are discovered and offered as a multi-select list with an All option; nothing is analyzed until the user chooses.
expectations: Lists only tools/<name>/ folders that contain a package.json, and mentions any folder without one (such as tools/power-pages-blueprint-generator) without offering it
Asks with AskUserQuestion which tool(s) to analyze, allowing several tools or all tools
Doesn't start the analysis or read tool source in depth before the selection is made

evals.expected_output: A read-only analysis produces a proposal with current state, a prioritized plan with S/M/L effort, a per-step risk analysis and a summary; the approval question is asked, and no file is modified.
expectations: Modifies no file during the analysis: no npm install, no npm audit fix, no formatter, nothing written to docs/todos; checks git status before and after any build or test run

Covers structure, code quality (duplication, complexity, typing gaps, dead code, naming, error handling), dependencies, UI/UX consistency, performance and maintainability, and test coverage, citing file paths
Lists steps with IDs (S1, S2, ...), rationale, expected benefit, files, effort S/M/L and risk Low/Medium/High, in execution order
Gives mitigation and rollback for every Medium or High step and names breaking changes, treating a change to the byte-for-byte dataverse-gen output as breaking

Asks the user to choose Accept all, Accept selected steps only, Save as TODO only, or Reject (Request changes through the free-text answer), and doesn't start executing or write a TODO file before the answer

Checks findings that depend on Microsoft platform behavior (Dataverse Web API, Fluent UI v9 tokens) with the Microsoft Learn MCP Server (microsoft_docs_search, then microsoft_docs_fetch when needed) and cites the Learn URLs in the evidence and the Microsoft Learn references section

evals.prompt: Looks good, go ahead with S1 and S3 only.
evals.expected_output: Before any code change, docs/todos/refactoring-<tool-name>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md is written with the analysis and a TODO checklist; then only S1 and S3 are executed, in order, each verified with npm run build and npm test and committed separately; then the report is given and the same TODO file is updated without asking.
expectations: Writes docs/todos/refactoring-<tool-name>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md before touching any other file, with the header (tool, date, skill, 'Accepted selected steps: S1, S3', status Planned), a TODO checklist of every step marking S1 and S3 approved, and the full analysis
Checks that the working tree is clean apart from that TODO file, and creates a branch if on main, before the first step
Executes S1 and S3 only, flagging any dependency on an unselected step before starting
Runs npm run build and npm test in the tool folder after each step and records exit codes and test counts
Commits each step separately with a Conventional Commits message such as refactor(<tool-name>): ..., without staging the TODO file, and doesn't push
Updates the same TODO file without asking: status Executed, S1 and S3 ticked with their commit SHAs, the other steps left open, an Execution report and a Follow-up TODOs checklist
Ends by stating the saved file path

evals.prompt: Execute the plan. (The file docs/todos/refactoring-dataverse-early-bound-typescript-generator-2026-10-16.md already exists from this morning.)
evals.expected_output: The existing report isn't overwritten; the new one is saved with a sequence suffix.
expectations: Checks whether the target file exists before writing
Saves the new TODO file (in Phase 4, before any change) as refactoring-dataverse-early-bound-typescript-generator-2026-10-16-02.md (or the next free suffix), and later updates only that new file
Leaves the existing file and every other file in docs/todos unchanged

evals.prompt: Accept all. (During step S2, npm test fails with 3 failing tests in test/generator.test.ts.)
evals.expected_output: Execution stops at S2, the failure is reported with the likely cause, and the user is asked whether to fix forward, revert, skip or stop; later steps aren't run until the user decides.
expectations: Stops after the failing verification and doesn't continue to S3
Reports the failing tests, the exit code and a hypothesis for the cause
Asks whether to fix forward, revert the step, skip it or stop
Doesn't commit the failing step and doesn't weaken or update the tests or reference files to make them pass without approval

evals.prompt: Reject. I don't want any of these changes.
evals.expected_output: The skill ends without modifying anything, including no report file in docs/todos.
expectations: Makes no file change and no commit
Doesn't write a refactoring report to docs/todos
Confirms that nothing was changed

evals.prompt: Save it as a TODO, don't change anything yet.
evals.expected_output: The proposal is saved as docs/todos/refactoring-<tool-name>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md with every step as an open TODO; no other file is changed, nothing is committed, and the skill ends.
expectations: Writes only the new TODO file in docs/todos, never overwriting an existing one
The file has the header with decision 'Saved as TODO only' and status 'Saved as TODO, no changes made', a TODO checklist with every step open, and the full analysis
Makes no change to tool code, config, docs or other files and makes no commit
Doesn't start execution, and ends by stating the saved file path and that nothing else changed

evals.prompt: Refactor dataverse-early-bound-typescript-generator. (No Microsoft Learn MCP server is configured in this session.)
evals.expected_output: The read-only analysis and the approval question still happen; the user is told the Microsoft Learn MCP Server is not available, with how to add it, and findings that would need Learn are marked "Microsoft Learn not checked" instead of stated from memory.
expectations: Says the Microsoft Learn MCP Server is not available and shows how to add it (https://learn.microsoft.com/api/mcp), without changing any MCP configuration itself
Marks findings about Microsoft platform behavior as "Microsoft Learn not checked" rather than presenting unverified API details as fact
Still completes the read-only analysis and asks the approval question without modifying any file
